messages.body_plain:
Hi all.
Maybe it's irrelevant. But I think the digest might want to mention that, Hadley Wickham, the author who created ggplot2, dplyr, tidyverse, etc, had just won the COPSS Presidents' Award at the 2019 Joint Statistical Meeting (JSM) in Denver, CO on July 31.. The COPSS Presidents' Award, by the way, is what we statisticians call "Nobel Prize of Statistics".

https://www.stat.iastate.edu/hadley-wickham-isu-alum-receives-cops-award

Congratulations to Hadley!

Yanlei

messages.subject_clean: how to define the color of different types in bidirectional bar chart
messages.body_plain:
I'm trying to apply different colors for type "down" and type "up". How can I define the specific color the type for down (blue) and type up (red)? Thank you in advance for any advice!

The following is my data:

     category| number| type;
     a|-1|down; b|-4|down; a|30|up; b|22|up.

I tried to use `scale_fill_manual` in my example, but it seems to be used for all single direction bar charts in those examples I could find. I wonder how to use scale_fill_manual for bidirectional bar chart. Below is the code I used. I am fairly new to R. I appreciate any comments.

    testData = read.csv("C:/Users/K/Desktop/example001.csv")
    library(ggplot2)
    library(scales)
    ggplot(data = testData,
           aes(x = category, y = number,
           fill = factor(type))) +
      geom_bar(position = "identity", stat = "identity", width = 0.5) +
      coord_flip() +
      labs(title = "example001") +
      ylim(-50, 50)

what I want is downregulation for blue; upregulation for red in the chart, not like the attached image

messages.subject: Re: how to define the color of different types in bidirectional bar chart
messages.subject_clean: how to define the color of different types in bidirectional bar chart
messages.body_plain:
Make type a factor before you feed it into ggplot is usually how I do it. Something like:

library(tidyverse)

testData <- read.csv("C:/Users/K/Desktop/example001.csv")

testData %>%
mutate(type = factor(type, levels = c("up", "down")) %>%
ggplot(data = .,

       aes(x = category, y = number,

       fill = type)) +

      geom_bar(position = "identity", stat = "identity", width = 0.5) +
      coord_flip() +
      labs(title = "example001") +

      ylim(-50, 50) +
scale_fill_manual(values=c("red","blue"))

I didn't test this because I'm too lazy to copy your table into R. Use dput() next time to share your data. It allows us to copy and replicate your input into R very easily. Or attach the CSV that you read in.

HTH,
B

messages.body_plain:
Dear group members,

Thanks,
Yong

+ geom_text(aes(y=label_y,label=Weight),vjust=1.5,colour="white")
I think the ggplot2 has some problem ,does anyone can solve it?(top panel is what I did. bottom is the book provided)

messages.subject: Re: image
messages.body_plain:
Hi,
When you add "position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5)" in the geom_text, you will get the result in the figure.

library(tidyverse)
library(gcookbook)
ce<-cabbage_exp%>%group_by(Date)%>%mutate(label_y=cumsum(Weight))

 ggplot(ce,aes(x=Date,y=Weight,fill=Cultivar))
+ geom_bar(stat="identity")

+ geom_text(aes(y=label_y,label=Weight),vjust=1.5,colour="white",position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5))

messages.subject: Re: image
messages.body_plain:
Your problem is the order in which C39 and C52 are plotting. In the Cookbook version, c39 is on stacked on the bottom; in your version, c39 is stacked on top. The geom_text() labels are printing in the same (correct) place in both versions.

This is normally corrected by reordering the factor levels. See the forecats package for easy ways to reorder factors.

This is also often a problem when using character data as categorical variables in ggplot2 plots; we often need to convert them to factors and order them for plotting.

- Tom
